answer.rationale: Constraints eliminate most candidates before evidence even matters: rollback_release is barred by a compliance ruling on the security patch (so memory_b1 and memory_b6, however well supported, are inapplicable); regional_failover (memory_b2) recovered latency in March but that was a read/latency degradation, and shifting regions during peak heavy settlement writes risks exactly the failure the objective forbids — lost or duplicated in-flight writes; enable_circuit_breaker (memory_b4) worked when a partner dependency was the fault domain, but here the write path itself is degrading, so failing fast would shed customer writes rather than protect them. That leaves relieving primary-node contention or adding headroom. memory_b5 is the closest structural match — it describes read load on the primary being displaced to replicas with transactional write latency recovering — and it is the only inherited memory whose mechanism directly targets write-path contention, so I want its source record to confirm the causal claim was actually measured (write latency recovered because of the reroute) rather than coincident with some other fix. memory_b3 is my fallback and worth verifying because add_capacity was validated ahead of a peak with lead time; if the source shows provisioning took hours to take effect, it is disqualified as a mid-incident lever and my choice is forced. Two caveats I am not resolving: I have no memory covering a 5x sustained climb on the write path specifically, and a release went out 2 hours ago that cannot be reverted — the latency may be caused by that patch, in which case read offloading only buys headroom and does not fix the root cause. Downstream value risk: moving report and dashboard queries to replicas introduces replication lag into anything reading them, which for a payments provider means reconciliation, settlement reporting, and possibly compliance or fraud checks could silently read stale balances; that must be gated, not assumed harmless. So I am running this as a small guarded test — reroute one clearly non-authoritative query class first, watch primary write p99 and replica lag together, and hold the capacity request for the next window rather than spending the single intervention on a lever whose latency-to-effect I have not yet confirmed.
